raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

NixlConnector pull with a smaller `--block-size` on P than on D writes wrong KV on D, or crashes D when a rank holds fewer KV heads than `block_size_ratio`. The receive post-process indexes attention views as `[B, N, H, D]`; since #44455 they are `[B, H, N, 2*D]` on every layout.

- `kv_postprocess_blksize_on_receive`: drop the two "physical order" permutes. On `LBHNC` they scramble every received block; with fewer heads than `block_size_ratio` the reshape fails.
- `post_process_device_kv_on_receive`: zero the untransferred tail along the token dim, not the head dim.
- `kv_postprocess_blksize_and_layout_on_receive` (`enable_permute_local_kv`): read the received bytes in memory order before viewing them as the remote's head-major blocks. It now also serves ratio 1 and replaces `kv_postprocess_layout_on_receive`, which had the same bug and a 5-D branch from #47791 that is dead since #51718.
- `enable_permute_local_kv` is enabled only for a local `LBNHC` cache; any other local layout (e.g. head-major `BLHNC`) now fails the handshake instead of receiving wrong KV.
- HMA groups alias the same KV tensors, but each group's block ids went through every attention view, regrouping a block once per aliasing group. Each group now uses its own views.
- `LBNHC`/`BLNHC` receive the remote sub-blocks in token order; only `is_block_contiguous` layouts are regrouped.

Block lists that start or end at different tokens on P and D are paired in #59746. No other open PR changes the receive post-process.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py -k test_post_process_zeroes_untransferred_tail
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py -k test_handshake_fails_on_kv_cache_layout_mismatch
```

The test now holds distinct values in a `[B, H, N, C]` cache with fewer KV heads than the ratio, aliased by two attention groups, on `LBHNC`, `LBNHC` and `LBNHC` + `enable_permute_local_kv`.

GB10: P and D on one GPU, pull, greedy, `--enforce-eager`. Each run is compared with P and D both at D's block size, without `enable_permute_local_kv`; D loads the whole prompt over NIXL, except the last token on GDN or with #59330.

## Test Result

CPU, main `0cbac6cd13`: the 3 cases pass, and reverting any one fix fails at least one of them. Other NIXL unit tests are unchanged.

GB10, main `0cbac6cd13`:
- Qwen3-0.6B, FLASH_ATTN, `LBHNC`, P 16 / D 64: 0/6 outputs match.
- `LBHNC` P to `LBNHC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`, 64/64: 0/6.
- Gemma-4-E2B-it, TRITON_ATTN, 1 KV head, 16/64: D's EngineCore fails with `shape '[-1, 4, 128, 0, 512]' is invalid`.

GB10, this PR at `ef0cc618a0` on main `0cbac6cd13`, logprobs bitwise equal:
- Qwen3-0.6B 16/64 on `LBHNC`, `BLHNC`, `LBNHC`, and `LBHNC` P to `LBNHC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`, the last also at 64/64: 6/6 each.
- Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN), FLASH_ATTN, 544/1088: 6/6, also with two attention groups forced by a local grouping hook.
- Gemma-4-E2B-it 16/64 no longer crashes; 4/7 outputs still differ in text. With #59746 and #59330: 7/7.

GB10, main `dd30786fef` + this PR's files at `0ccf122132`, MiniCPM5-2B (2 KV heads), `LBHNC` P to `BLHNC` D with `enable_permute_local_kv`: main crashes D at 16/64; without the handshake check, 0/4 outputs match at 16/64 and 64/64 with no error. With it, the handshake fails and D keeps serving; an `LBNHC` D stays bitwise equal (4/4) at both.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, patch and tests. I reviewed every changed line.

"""Convert received HND blocks into the local NHD block layout.

The remote block is heads-first and remote_block_size <= local block_size
(block_size_ratio >= 1); the local cache must be tokens-first within a block
(e.g. LBNHC, BLNHC).
"""

```suggestion
    _, H, N, C = cache.shape
    assert cache.stride()[1:] == (C, H * C, 1), "expected local NHD block"
    
    blocks_to_update = cache.index_select(0, indices)
```
Maybe add this assertion to fail loudly in case it was misused.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
@Dao007forever I don't think this is the right place to check. It should be checked on startup and isn't related to this PR.  Maybe that's something you could tackle!

We can't check on startup as this is only available when decode knows about prefill layout (we don't know if we will run this code path until then? Setting enable_permute_local_kv doesn't mean we need this either, as block_size_ratio could be 1)

This is simple so please add it so it can't fail silently like before?

Thanks @Dao007forever, your review is what surfaced this. With this PR, a head-major local cache was silently permuted into wrong KV, so I added a check at the handshake in 0ccf122132: only a local `LBNHC` cache enables the permute now, and any other layout fails the handshake.

We can't check on startup as this is only available when decode knows about prefill layout (we don't know if we will run this code path until then? Setting enable_permute_local_kv doesn't mean we need this either, as block_size_ratio could be 1)

This is simple so please add it so it can't fail silently like before?

Thanks @Dao007forever, your review is what surfaced this. With this PR, a head-major local cache was silently permuted into wrong KV, so I added a check at the handshake in 0ccf122132: only a local `LBNHC` cache enables the permute now, and any other layout fails the handshake.
